ideas.description: Replace the template with a full airbench port in submissions/arena/. Architecture: a frozen 2x2 patch-whitening first conv (eigenvectors computed in prepare from training images), Dirac-initialized convs, widths 128/384/576 with 3 convs per group, BN with a 64x bias LR, and a GAP+linear head scaled for 100 classes. Optimizer: Nesterov SGD at batch 1024 with lr 9.0 (airbench scaling), wd 0.012, Lookahead and a triangular LR. Training: label smoothing 0.3, alternating flip, random crop with 2 px translate, 8.5 epochs, no TTA. The full uint8 dataset lives on the GPU with augmentation done there. Use fp16 autocast and channels_last. torch.compile the train step in build and warm it up on synthetic data; use drop_last so batch shapes stay fixed. Eval uses an uncompiled (or dynamic=True) path so any B from 1 to 1024 avoids slow recompiles. Log prepare and train time separately.
ideas.expected: First feasible-or-near-miss run: accuracy 0.750-0.758 and time 8-10 s (versus 0.012 and 0.10 s for the infeasible baseline). If accuracy is >=0.753 this becomes the incumbent. If it is a near-miss, the 9.5-epoch idea is the fix.

ideas.description: Same as the airbench port, with only the epoch count raised from 8.5 to 9.5. The triangular LR schedule stretches to match, and nothing else changes. This hedges the thin margin that the TTA ban leaves.
ideas.expected: Accuracy rises by >=0.4 pp, to >=0.756, and time rises by <=12% (about +1 s). It should be safely feasible even if 8.5 epochs misses 0.753.

ideas.description: Re-run the current incumbent airbench config unchanged, as a pure replicate, and record per-seed accuracies and per-trial prepare/train times. This calibrates the noise floor that every later delta is judged against.
ideas.expected: 3-seed mean accuracy within ±0.2 pp of the first run, time within ±3%, per-seed std <=0.35 pp. The metrics should not improve; the value is information only.

ideas.description: On the feasible airbench incumbent, widen the last group from 576 to 768 channels (128/384/768) and cut epochs from the incumbent count to 7.5, with the LR schedule rescaled. Everything else is held fixed.
ideas.expected: Accuracy within ±0.3 pp of the incumbent, and time within ±5% of it. If it is >5% faster and still >=0.753, H1.5 is refuted and the frontier moves toward wider and shorter.

ideas.description: On the incumbent, compute the patch-whitening covariance from a random 5000-image subset (drawn with the trial-seeded generator inside prepare) instead of all 50k. Also make the dataset transfer a single bulk uint8 copy to the GPU, with normalization fused into the train step. Report prepare time.
ideas.expected: Prepare time drops by >=0.1 s, to <=0.5 s in total, so total time falls by about 1-3%. Accuracy within ±0.2 pp.

ideas.description: Throughput ablation on the incumbent: switch the torch.compile mode from default to max-autotune, with autotuning done fully in the untimed build on synthetic batches of the exact training shapes (full batch plus any eval shapes used in train). Check with TORCH_LOGS=recompiles that zero recompiles happen in the timed region, which also covers H3.2.1.
ideas.expected: Train time per epoch drops by 5-15% (total time about -0.5 to -1.2 s), and accuracy is unchanged within noise. If the recompiles log shows extra recompiles, removing them should save >=0.5 s.

ideas.description: Explore: on the incumbent architecture, replace Nesterov SGD on the conv weights with Muon (lr ~0.24, momentum 0.6, 3 Newton-Schulz steps, batch 2000). Biases, BN and the head stay on SGD. Use the same epoch budget, tuned so wall time matches the SGD incumbent.
ideas.expected: The prior favours SGD: accuracy >=0.3 pp below the incumbent at equal time. Upside case: Muon matches accuracy in >=10% less time, which would refute H1.4 and open a new optimizer branch.

ideas.description: Explore: on the incumbent, train the first ~50% of epochs on 24 px random crops (downscaled from 32 px on the GPU), then 32 px for the rest. Compile and warm up both shapes in build.
ideas.expected: Train time drops by about 15-20%, and accuracy drops by 0.2-0.6 pp. The run is useful only if the drop is <=0.3 pp. Otherwise, pair it with +0.5 epoch.

structured_output.summary: The queue was empty and only the infeasible template baseline has run, so the top priority is getting a first feasible run. Two priority-5 ideas do that: the airbench port at 8.5 epochs (H1.1.1) and a 9.5-epoch version as a hedge for the thin margin without TTA (H1.1.2). Next comes a replicate run to calibrate noise (H1.1.3). After that, three exploit refinements: wider and shorter training (H1.5.1), a cheaper prepare via subset whitening (H3.1.1), and max-autotune with a zero-recompile check (H2.2.1/H3.2.1). Two explore ideas round out the queue: Muon (H1.4.1) and progressive resizing (H2.3.1). Flip, label-smoothing, Cutout and data-filtering ablations are held back until a feasible incumbent exists. Nothing was dropped.
